agree.reason: The tone is calm and cooperative, but a manager who thinks the association is a few loud people gets nothing that changes her mind: there is no two-thirds share, no dialysis case and no specific dated ask, and the letter offers nothing in return.

honest.reason: Most claims follow the brief, but 'They miss medical appointments' and 'some of them can't leave their apartments at all' are stated as general facts that the brief does not supply.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw numbers are repeated without being worked: 74 of 112 is two-thirds of households, 41 days is roughly one day in eight so far this year, and a June estimate of 6–8 weeks means the part was due by August, yet the letter derives none of these.

right_comparison.reason: The letter never says what happens if nothing changes, such as another 12-day outage while the part is still 'on order', and it doesn't use the record of 41 outage days as a trend.

qualification.reason: 'Firm, written timeline' and 'within 30 days' are the only limits, and neither names a date or says what the association will do if it is missed, even though the 1st-of-month posting and the Channel 7 visit were available as leverage.

objections.reason: It deals well with the inspection certificate by separating safety from reliability, but it leaves the 'a few loud people' view unanswered when 74 of 112 households would answer it.

fit.reason: It is an open letter of about the right length, but the brackets left for names, building and date make it unready to post or send to TV as it stands.
